canonical.title: Find the City With the Smallest Number of Neighbors at a Threshold Distance
canonical.sourceFilePath: 13. Graphs/4. Shortest Path Problems/10. Find city with smallest number of neighbours.cpp

narrative.title: Siting the Quietest Relay Depot
narrative.scenario: A telco must site its failover depot in the city that would serve the fewest neighbours — measured as cities reachable by any route totalling at most a given latency budget. Ties are broken deliberately: among the quietest candidates, the greatest city id wins. Every city's full reach map is needed before the choice can be made.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer n (cities 0..n-1), a list edges where [u, v, w] is a bidirectional weighted link, and distanceThreshold.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the city with the fewest reachable cities within distanceThreshold; break ties by choosing the greatest city id.

testCases.explanation: Cities 0 and 3 both reach two neighbours within budget; the tie favours the greater id, 3.
City 0 reaches only city 1 within budget 2 — one neighbour, fewer than anyone else.

hintLevels: Level 1: You need every city's reach map, not just one — a shortest-path run per city.
Level 2: For each source, Dijkstra once, then count destinations within the budget.
Level 3: Track (count, city) with ascending-count then descending-id preference when picking the winner.
